t: For provisions of law which reduce spending for fiscal 1981 in small business programs in satisfaction of the reconciliation requirements imposed by sections 3(a)(6) and 3(a)(19) of H. Con. Res. 307 (96th Congress), see Public Law 96–302 (the Small Business Development Act of 1980).

fable.w: This section is only a cross-reference pointing to Public Law 96-302 for spending reductions that satisfy reconciliation requirements of a congressional resolution. The tempting reading is that the reference to reconciliation requirements signals a procedural interaction, but that is internal congressional budget process and involves no outside party in any federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with non-federal entities, or right to sue.

qwen_block.w: This section is a cross-reference directing the reader to another statute (Public Law 96–302) for details on spending reductions. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely administrative and legislative in nature.

opus.w: This section is only a cross-reference note. It points readers to Public Law 96–302 for 1981 small business spending cuts made to meet a congressional budget resolution. The 'reconciliation requirements' are part of Congress's internal budget process, so every actor is inside the federal government. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** "Reconciliation requirements imposed by... H. Con. Res. 307" sounds like a formal process. But budget reconciliation happens entirely inside Congress, which is part of the federal government. The section is only a cross-reference note pointing to spending cuts in another law. No one outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any decision.

It does not establish any mechanism for outside parties to consult with, comment on, or participate in federal decision-making. The mention of 'small business programs' refers to the subject matter of the spending cuts, not a participatory process defined in this text.

It does not describe any specific process of consultation, comment, or coordination with outsiders in this section. It is a legislative housekeeping provision.
